subject: How to make the MESH boundary extend inwards？

messages.author: 8a4b47298f2cd317
messages.subject: How to make the MESH boundary extend inwards？
parts:
Hello!
When I used the following code for the construction of the mesh, I found that the dense triangular mesh does not cover my study area (the part within the green boundary). In the middle of the study area, the dense triangular mesh was replaced by a sparse triangular mesh.
my code:
boundary_coords = as.matrix(boundary_coords)
bnd = inla.nonconvex.hull(boundary_coords)
mesh = inla.mesh.2d(boundary=bnd,max.edge=c(0.03,0.1),cutoff=0.01,offset=-0.2)
In this, the green dots are the boundary.
My question is how to change the code to make the centre of my study area also a dense triangular mesh instead of a sparse one?
Thanks for your help!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to make the MESH boundary extend inwards？
parts:
The inla.nonconvex.hull algorithm constructs a buffer region around the given point set, so in this case you can solve it by adding a point in the middle (where the hole appeared) to the point set you’re giving to inla.nonconvex.hull, or to add the red dots from you plot to it; since there are several of the in the hole, that should get rid of it.

There’s also a new algorithm that will be available in the new fmesher package that avoids this issue when provided with a polygon as input; it’s already available via the inlabru development package. See
https://inlabru-org.github.io/inlabru/reference/fm_nonconvex_hull.html

Finn
